title: Warren Buffett at Georgetown 2013: temperament, circle of competence, and America's long-run optimism
summary: In a 2013 Georgetown conversation with Brian Moynihan, Buffett explains why temperament beats IQ in investing, why you only need to swing at a few pitches, and why he stays optimistic about America despite panics. He also covers the Giving Pledge, inequality, and the GEICO and Heinz deals.

principles.text: Investing success depends on temperament, not a sky-high IQ; ignore the crowd and judge the facts.
principles.quote: it doesn't take a high iq to figure out that they're cheap but it does take a temperament that's willing to step up and actually act

principles.text: Stay inside your circle of competence; you only need to be right on a few businesses.
principles.quote: it's a terrible mistake to think you have to have an opinion on everything you only have to have an opinion on a few things

principles.text: Investing has no called strikes: wait for the right pitch and swing only when you understand the business and like the price.
principles.quote: in investing there's no called strikes

principles.text: Humans repeat the same mistakes: greed builds slowly, fear hits all at once, so panics will recur.
principles.quote: when they get fearful it happens all at once i mean when everybody wants when people get scared they all want to leave at one time

principles.text: Bet on America's long-run progress despite recessions and occasional panics.
principles.quote: don't ever worry about america it'll tell you you're in the right place

principles.text: Pick businesses with simple, durable, travelling products and think in per-unit economics, like Coca-Cola's penny.
principles.quote: i like products that travel well
